Several days: about 33 min of Rotten Charges + up to 15 min of fighting for each of the four bosses (20 h cooldown each) and up to 25 min for Bakragore (cooldown of 2 days and 20 hours)

You receive the base {wiki:Decaying Defender Outfits|Decaying Defender} outfit and permission to make {wiki:Crimson Offering|Crimson Offerings} in exchange for {wiki:Sanguine Set|Sanguine Set} equipment.

The addons require a {item:Cursed Wood} (Ichgahal) and a {item:Darklight Geode} (Chagorz).

Bakragore's Burden and the essences of Bakragore's children
With the final taint (after you kill Bakragore) the four children can drop their essences, which you can sacrifice before fighting Bakragore again.
The only way to get the Grand Sanguine versions of the weapons.

The four children can be killed in **any order** (the taints always arrive in the same order). The order most players consider best: **Murcion** (Jaded Roots) → **Vemiath** (Darklight Core) → **Chagorz** (Gloom Pillars) → **Ichgahal** (Putrefactory), leaving the easiest boss for when you already have three taints.
Each of Bakragore's children has a **20-hour** cooldown and a **15-minute** fight; Bakragore has a cooldown of **2 days and 20 hours** and a **25-minute** fight. Plan several days with the same team.
In each area and **before each fight**, the Rotten Charges counter of **all** members must reach 100. Alone it takes 33 minutes; use each area's mechanics to speed it up.

The team's taint level is that of the member with the **fewest** taints. To earn a taint in a fight you must have that same minimum number, not yet have that boss's taint and deal damage to the boss. Try to always do the quest with the same team.

Paladins: avoid diagonal steps and use {wiki:Powerful Vibrancy|Powerful Vibrancy}; all bosses cast {wiki:Paralyse|Paralyse} constantly and some heal a lot if they stand still. Knights: use the {item:Necklace of the Deep} almost all the time, because of the heavy Life Drain from the {creature:Elder Bloodjaw|Elder Bloodjaws}.
The mechanics are essential: failing them makes the boss harder to kill or harms the whole team. The lower the team's level, the more important it is to follow them.
1. Get to Drefia and talk to Torkada
The quest begins in Drefia, the old necromancer city west of Darashia. {npc:Torkada}, in the service of the Inquisition, is right at the entrance, on the mountain.

Travel to **Darashia**: by boat ({npc:Petros} connects Darashia with Venore, Ankrahmun, Port Hope, Liberty Bay, Yalahar, Issavi, Krailos and Gray Island; to that city's captain say {key:hi}, {key:darashia} and {key:yes} and you arrive at Petros's harbour) or by magic carpet (you arrive at {npc:Chemar}). From Thais, Carlin, Edron or Ab'Dendriel there is no direct boat: go via Venore first.

Leave Darashia heading **west**, towards the mountains that separate Ankrahmun, Darashia, Drefia and Tiquanda. Use the {item:Rope} at this spot {coord:33048,32429,7} to climb up (you can also come through the pass between Darashia and Ankrahmun). {wiki:Drefia|Drefia} is on the other side, to the west ({coord:33018,32443,7}).
Rope spot to climb up to Drefia
There are many {creature:Scorpion|Scorpions} on the mountain; at this level they are not dangerous, but they poison you.

Talk to {npc:Torkada}: say {key:hi}, {key:expedition}, {key:mission} and {key:yes}. He tells you that some adventurers from an Inquisition expedition found the entrance to an evil temple, too filthy even by Drefia's standards, and sealed the entrance to contain the corruption. When you accept the mission to eradicate the evil inside, he blesses you and you are then able to enter the temple.
The temple is north-west of Torkada and can only be entered with {spell:Levitate}. Inside, {npc:A Bloodshade} guards the pool of blood that serves as a portal to the blood realm.
Go up at the Levitate spot
Go to the {spell:Levitate} spot **north-west** of Torkada and go up with *exani hur up*.
Go down to the door between the pillars

Get past the 2 {creature:Ghoul|Ghouls}, go down the stairs and then down the hole. Go down again via the stairs just to the **north-east** and continue **south-west** to a door between two limestone pillars. Go through the door: {npc:A Bloodshade} is right at the entrance of the room.
A Bloodshade (floor -2, two floors below the Levitate spot)
Keep the {item:Rope}: you will need it to climb back up through this hole when you leave.

Talk to {npc:A Bloodshade}: say {key:hi} and {key:quest}. He explains that the temple guards the entrance to the blood realm of the blood god, his master, which is being corrupted by a festering offspring, a parody of the god's former glory. To enter you must sacrifice **2 {item:Bloody Tears}** or **5,000,000 gp**.
Do **not** step into the pool of blood before making the sacrifice: you take {wiki:Agony Damage|Agony Damage}, which removes a percentage of your health.

**With tears:** with the 2 {item:Bloody Tears} on you, use the sacrifice plate **twice** (you may need to click several times until the tears are consumed). **With gold:** choose the {key:detour} option in the conversation with {npc:A Bloodshade} to pay the 5,000,000 gp. After that, the pool of blood works as a portal.

Step into the pool of blood. You arrive at the {wiki:Blood Vestibule|Blood Vestibule}, the entrance to the four Rotten Blood hunting areas, part of the blood realm of the Sanguine Lord, the blood god.

Right at the entrance of the Blood Vestibule, talk to {npc:A Bloodshade} again: say {key:hi} and {key:quest}. You must kill the **two pairs of evil twins** lurking in the areas ahead; only after the four victories does the way open to {creature:Bakragore}, the filthy presence that desecrates this realm. If you want the full explanation, continue with {key:twins}, {key:beginning}, {key:sacrifice}, {key:decay}, {key:prevail} and {key:cost}: each victory leaves a taint in you, a corruption that brings penalties, but only inside the contaminated areas.

Explore the Blood Vestibule: ahead there are **four rooms**, each with a {item:Spheric Teleporter}. Use the one in each room to go to one of the four hunting areas (Jaded Roots, Darklight Core, Gloom Pillars and Putrefactory). The general coordinates of each area are in the following sections, so you can confirm where you have arrived.
3. Common mechanics: Rotten Charges and Bakragore's Taints

Before you start killing the bosses it is very important to understand these two mechanics. The wiki does not give the exact position of the lever rooms inside each area, nor the exits from the areas and boss rooms; each section gives the area's general coordinates.

In each area, and **every time the team wants to fight a boss**, the {wiki:Rotten Charge (Counter)|Rotten Charges} counter of **all** members must reach **100** before they can enter the boss's lever room. The counter appears next to the character's name (upward arrow icon), just above the taints counter (blood drop icon). It rises on its own while you are in the hunting area: 1 charge every 20 seconds, full in **33 minutes**. Each area has its own mechanics to speed it up (see each section).

Each of Bakragore's children you kill gives a {wiki:Bakragore's Taints|Bakragore's Taint} to the whole team. Killing the same boss again does **not** give a new taint, so to have all four you must kill all four bosses. The taints **always arrive in the same order**, whichever boss is killed, and only take effect inside the Rotten Blood areas:
Melee monsters have a 6% chance to swap positions with you (within a certain radius). An effect on your tile warns you 2 seconds beforehand.
When a monster dies, there is a 6.25% chance of a {creature:Bloodjaw} spawning from the corpse. In boss fights an extra {creature:Elder Bloodjaw} appears.
Monsters can root you and attack with a 4th element: Death (Jaded Roots), Earth (Putrefactory), Energy (Gloom Pillars) or Fire (Darklight Core).
You take **+14%** damage from all sources in the Rotten Blood.
How taints work in a team

The team's taint level is that of the member with the **fewest** taints. To earn a taint in a fight you must: have that minimum number of taints, not yet have that boss's taint and **deal damage** to the boss. Example: if four players have two taints (Murcion and Vemiath) and a fifth has none, the team fights without taints and, on killing Ichgahal, only the fifth player gains a taint.
Anyone who does not hit the boss does not receive that fight's taint. Make sure everyone deals damage.

The taints also bring advantages: each one gives a 7.8% chance of a second loot roll on normal monsters (7.8% → 15.6% → 23.4% → 31.2% → 39%), increases the experience from the area's monsters, gives a chance of {item:Tainted Heart|Tainted Hearts} and {item:Darklight Heart|Darklight Hearts} as loot from normal monsters and increases the chance of Bakragore's four children dropping a {item:Bag You Covet}.
You can kill the bosses in any order you like. Because of the difficulty of the areas and bosses, the most common order is this:

Unlike most older fights, here the **Paladin** is the main blocker. All bosses fight with at least two {creature:Elder Bloodjaw|Elder Bloodjaws} (more, depending on the team's taints), and all of them cast {wiki:Paralyse|Paralyse} constantly. Paladins: avoid diagonal steps and use {wiki:Powerful Vibrancy|Powerful Vibrancy}. Knights: use the {item:Necklace of the Deep} almost all the time because of the Elder Bloodjaws' Life Drain. Each of Bakragore's children has a **20-hour** cooldown and a **15-minute** fight.
One of the hardest fights, because of the small room. The monsters in this area deal Earth, Physical and Fire damage (and Death to those with 3+ taints) and are weak to Energy, Ice and Holy.

In the Blood Vestibule, use the {item:Spheric Teleporter} that leads to the {wiki:Jaded Roots|Jaded Roots}. Here you hunt {creature:Sopping Corpus}, {creature:Oozing Corpus}, {creature:Mycobiontic Beetle} and {creature:Bloated Man-Maggot}.
Earth, Physical, Fire (and Death with 3+ taints)
Watch out for the Decaying Totems

When a monster dies, there is a chance that a {creature:Decaying Totem} appears. It casts **four rings in a row** in widening waves, each one dealing heavy damage, and then disappears. Move away from it as soon as it appears.
Speed up the Rotten Charges counter
To fill the 100 Rotten Charges faster:
Use {item:Organic Acid} on a {item:Small Spore Reservoir}

The {item:Organic Acid} drops from the area's monsters ({creature:Sopping Corpus}, {creature:Oozing Corpus}, {creature:Mycobiontic Beetle} and {creature:Bloated Man-Maggot}). Each player can only use the same {item:Spore Reservoir} once every 10 minutes.
With **everyone's** counter at 100, enter the boss's lever room and use the lever to face {creature:Murcion} (600,000 HP). You have **15 minutes**; the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown.
Do not step on the Mould trails

Murcion leaves {item:Mould (Field)|Mould} trails on the ground wherever he walks or stands. If a player steps on or stands in a trail, they lose **12.5% of their max health per second** in {wiki:Agony Damage|Agony Damage}. If the **boss** steps on or stands in his own trails, he **heals a lot** (15,000+). The boss must always walk onto clean ground.
Never leave Murcion standing on the trails: lower-level teams cannot withstand several heals like these and run out of time to kill him.

The boss fights with two {creature:Elder Bloodjaw|Elder Bloodjaws} (not counting the extra ones from taints). Throughout the fight he summons {creature:Mushroom|Mushrooms} at random around him, up to 8 at a time. They explode after a while or when someone gets close, dealing **2,500+ Life Drain** in a small area.

The **Paladin** immediately pulls Murcion's target and runs in a circle, as wide as possible. Pace is everything: if they run too fast, they complete the lap before the Mould trails disappear; if they run too slowly, the boss ends up healing on his own trail.

The shooters never get close to the boss, so as not to draw his target. If the boss switches target to a shooter, that player **immediately runs in the same direction** the Paladin was running, so that Murcion keeps walking the right way.

The **Knight** uses {spell:Challenge} on the Elder Bloodjaws as soon as they appear and runs around the room in the same direction as the Paladin, about **half a lap behind**, so as to always be on the opposite side. Along the way, they pass close to the Mushrooms to pop them and clear the path for the Paladin's next lap.
Find a balance: the boss has a limit of active Mushrooms. Leaving some alive stops him from summoning so many that he gets stuck between them, standing still and healing several times in a row.

Open Murcion's corpse. You receive a Bakragore's Taint (the 1st, if it is your first boss) and 3,250,000 experience. Besides Crystal Coins, potions, gems and ambers, he can drop {item:Putrefactive Figurine}, {item:Spiritual Horseshoe}, {item:Bag You Covet} and, with the final taint, {item:The Essence of Murcion}.

The wiki does not describe the exit from the boss room or from the Jaded Roots. Go back to the point where the {item:Spheric Teleporter} dropped you in the area and return that way to the Blood Vestibule; if you cannot find an exit, use a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} to return to your city's temple. To leave for good, follow the steps "Leave the Blood Vestibule" and "Leave the temple and Drefia" in section 9.

The {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} takes you to your temple, but it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block: wait for the combat block to wear off before using it.
The monsters in this area deal Energy, Physical and Ice damage (and Fire to those with 3+ taints) and are weak to Earth, Fire and Physical.

In the Blood Vestibule, use the {item:Spheric Teleporter} that leads to the {wiki:Darklight Core|Darklight Core}. Here you hunt {creature:Walking Pillar}, {creature:Darklight Matter}, {creature:Darklight Source} and {creature:Darklight Striker}.
Energy, Physical, Ice (and Fire with 3+ taints)

The monsters in this area can place a {item:Darkfield} under you. It is similar to a Fire Field, but deals heavy {wiki:Agony Damage|Agony Damage}. It can only be destroyed with {item:Destroy Field Rune|Destroy Field Runes}, and it always hits the initial target.
Speed up the Rotten Charges counter
To fill the 100 Rotten Charges faster:
Use {item:Unstable Darklight Matter} on pools of blood
Use {item:Yellow Darklight Matter} on pools of blood

{item:Unstable Darklight Matter} drops from {creature:Darklight Striker|Darklight Strikers} and {creature:Darklight Matter}; {item:Yellow Darklight Matter} drops from {creature:Walking Pillar|Walking Pillars} and {creature:Darklight Source|Darklight Sources}. Use them straight away: they disappear after a few minutes. The {item:Darklight Obelisk} breaks when someone uses it and comes back 10 seconds later; each player can only use the same obelisk once every 10 minutes.

With **everyone's** counter at 100, enter the lever room and use the lever to face {creature:Vemiath} (600,000 HP), Chagorz's twin. You have **15 minutes**; the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown. Protect yourself from **Energy**.

During the fight you have a counter next to your name (white X icon) that rises by **2 per second** up to **21**. At its maximum, you take **15% of your max health** in Agony Damage per second. Each step you take "drops" a charge on the ground as a {item:Darklight Spark} and lowers the counter by 1. Stepping on or standing in a Darklight Spark takes **3% of your max health** per second. After 3 seconds, the Sparks turn into {item:Darklight Field|Darklight Fields}, which last 2 seconds and also take 3% as soon as you step on them. You can take up to 18% per second if you are not careful: keep moving, but do not step on your own trails.
Charge counter icon during the fight
Vemiath heals **200 HP** for each Darklight Spark and **400 HP** for each Darklight Field he steps on.
Avoid the Pillars of Dark Energy

The boss summons up to 8 {creature:Pillar of Dark Energy|Pillars of Dark Energy}. Each one chains whoever is next to it with **Energy** damage: never stand next to one, let alone several (the chains fire at the same time, with huge damage spikes). Whoever gets chained gains another counter (red ball icon, max 11) that drops by 1 per second and deals about **1,200 Energy** per tick.
Vemiath's beam triggers **all** the charges of that counter at once. If you have many, stay out of the boss's front.
Lead an Elder Bloodjaw onto the Rotten Charge

Every **90 seconds** a {wiki:Rotten Charge|Rotten Charge} appears in the centre of the room, lasting 15 seconds. You must get an {creature:Elder Bloodjaw} to step on it. **If none steps on it:** the room warns you at 6 seconds (*"The rotten charge is going to explode!"*) and at 10 (*"THE ROTTEN CHARGE WILL EXPLODE SOON!"*); at 15 it explodes and each player loses **40% of their max health**. **If an Elder Bloodjaw steps on it**, for 15 seconds: those nearby do not drop Sparks or Fields, the boss does not heal on the trails, all Elder Bloodjaws leave the room and the boss's resistances drop considerably. In return, the boss prepares a devastating blow on his current target, at 6 and at 12 seconds.
The boss shouts *"WILL ... PUNISH ... YOU!"* at the start of the mechanic and again after the 1st blow, and *"RAAAR!"* on the 2nd blow.

The most common strategy: the **Paladin** runs in circles with the boss in the **north** part of the room and the shooters split between the **west** and **east** sides. The **Knight** takes the Elder Bloodjaws and runs in circles with them in the **south** part. When the Rotten Charge appears, the Knight leads the Bloodjaws onto it and then pulls the boss to absorb the two blows. Then the Paladin picks up the boss again and everything repeats until Vemiath dies.

Open Vemiath's corpse. You receive the next taint and 3,250,000 experience. Besides Crystal Coins, potions and gems, he can drop {item:Vemiath's Infused Basalt}, {item:Darklight Figurine}, {item:Bag You Covet} and, with the final taint, {item:The Essence of Vemiath}.

As in the Jaded Roots, the wiki does not describe the exit: go back to the point where the {item:Spheric Teleporter} dropped you and return that way to the Blood Vestibule (or use a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll}). To leave for good, follow the steps "Leave the Blood Vestibule" and "Leave the temple and Drefia" in section 9.
The monsters in this area deal Holy, Fire and Earth damage (and Energy to those with 3+ taints) and are weak to Physical, Death and Energy.

In the Blood Vestibule, use the {item:Spheric Teleporter} that leads to the {wiki:Gloom Pillars|Gloom Pillars}. Here you hunt {creature:Darklight Emitter}, {creature:Darklight Construct}, {creature:Wandering Pillar} and {creature:Converter}.
Holy, Fire, Earth (and Energy with 3+ taints)
Watch out for the dark energy

In this area you absorb dark energy, on a counter of its own next to your name. When it reaches **100**, a painful chain fires on you (initial distance of 3 tiles, jumps of up to 6 tiles) that can jump to up to **5 targets** nearby, with more damage on each jump.
When your counter is close to 100, move away from your teammates.
Speed up the Rotten Charges counter
To fill the 100 Rotten Charges faster:
Use a {item:Darklight Obsidian Axe} on the pillars

The {item:Darklight Obsidian Axe} drops from the area's four monsters and disappears after a few minutes if you do not use it; use it on the stone pillars. The item page mentions 3 charges (60 seconds) per use, the spoiler 1. Each player can only use the same {item:Darklight Obelisk} once every 10 minutes.

With **everyone's** counter at 100, enter the lever room and use the lever to face {creature:Chagorz} (600,000 HP), Vemiath's twin. You have **15 minutes**; the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown. Protect yourself from **Fire** and **Energy**.

As with Vemiath, you have a counter (white X icon) that rises by **2 per second** up to **21**; at its maximum you take **15% of your max health** per second. Each step drops a charge on the ground as a {item:Darkfield} and lowers the counter by 1. The Darkfields last 3 seconds and take **3% of your max health** when you step on them, or per second while you stand on them. Keep moving, without stepping on your own trails.
Chagorz heals **375 HP** for each Darkfield he steps on.
Avoid the Pillars of Dark Energy

The boss summons up to 8 {creature:Pillar of Dark Energy|Pillars of Dark Energy}, which chain whoever is next to them with **Fire** damage. Never stand next to one (let alone several). Whoever gets chained gains the red ball counter (max 11), which drops by 1 per second and deals about **1,200 Fire** per tick.
Chagorz's beam triggers **all** those charges at once.
Lead an Elder Bloodjaw onto the Rotten Charge

Every **90 seconds** Chagorz drops a {wiki:Rotten Charge|Rotten Charge} in the centre of the room, lasting 15 seconds. **If no Elder Bloodjaw steps on it:** warnings at 6 and 10 seconds and, at 15, an explosion that takes **40% of max health** from each player. **If an Elder Bloodjaw steps on it**, for 15 seconds: those nearby do not drop Darkfields, the boss does not heal on the fields, the Elder Bloodjaws leave the room and the boss's resistances drop considerably; in return, the boss deals two devastating blows to his current target, at 6 and at 12 seconds (Knight: 5% and 10% of max health; Paladin, Druid or Sorcerer: 20% and 40%).
The shouts are the same as Vemiath's: *"WILL ... PUNISH ... YOU!"* at the start and after the 1st blow, *"RAAAR!"* on the 2nd.

Same as for Vemiath: the **Paladin** runs in circles with the boss in the **north** part, the shooters split between **west** and **east**, and the **Knight** runs with the Elder Bloodjaws in the **south** part. When the Rotten Charge appears, the Knight leads the Bloodjaws onto it and then pulls the boss to absorb the two blows; then the Paladin picks up the boss again.

Open Chagorz's corpse. You receive the next taint and 3,250,000 experience. Besides Crystal Coins, potions and gems, he can drop {item:Chagorz Igneous Obsidian}, {item:Darklight Figurine}, {item:Darklight Geode} (2nd Decaying Defender addon), {item:Bag You Covet} and, with the final taint, {item:The Essence of Chagorz}.

The wiki does not describe the way out: go back to the spot where the {item:Spheric Teleporter} left you and return that way to the Blood Vestibule (or use a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll}). To leave for good, follow the steps “Leave the Blood Vestibule” and “Leave the temple and Drefia” in section 9.

Probably the easiest boss of the quest, so leave it for last, when you already have three taints. The monsters in this area deal Death, Ice and Energy damage (and Earth to anyone with 3+ taints) and are weak to Holy, Earth and Fire.

In the Blood Vestibule, use the {item:Spheric Teleporter} that leads to the {wiki:Putrefactory|Putrefactory}. Here you hunt {creature:Oozing Carcass}, {creature:Sopping Carcass}, {creature:Rotten Man-Maggot} and {creature:Meandering Mushroom}.
Death, Ice and Earth (Earth because of the totems and the 3rd taint's attacks)

There are indestructible {creature:Radicular Totem|Radicular Totems} in every large room. They cast huge waves of **4,500 Earth damage** that reach very far (even beyond your screen), at set times and rotating direction: east, south, west and then north. Each creature that dies near a totem gives it a charge (you see the number next to its name), and each charge adds **+10%** to the damage.
You can block the waves with {item:Magic Wall Rune|Magic Walls}, but the monsters also break the walls: do not always count on them.
Speed up the Rotten Charges counter
To fill the 100 Rotten Charges faster:
Use a {item:Lichen Gobbler} on certain tiles on the **lower floor** of the area

The {item:Lichen Gobbler} drops from the four monsters in the area. It does not always work: sometimes it does not eat the tile and it can break at random. Each player can only use the same {item:Spore Reservoir} once every 10 minutes.

With **everyone's** counter at 100, enter the lever room and use the lever to face {creature:Ichgahal}, Murcion's twin. You have **15 minutes**; the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown. Protect yourself against **Life Drain** and **Death**.
Do not let the boss step on the fungi

Ichgahal leaves trails of {item:Spores} wherever it walks or stands. In this 1st state, touching them deals a little Agony Damage and a {wiki:Hexed|lesser hex}. After a few seconds they turn into {item:Volatile Funghi}: touching them deals a lot of Agony Damage and a **greater hex** for 15 seconds, and the funghi turns into a {item:Spore Cloud}, which is even more dangerous.
The boss heals **13,500 HP** for each Volatile Funghi it steps on and **27,000 HP** for each Spore Cloud. Always lead it onto clean ground.

It fights with two {creature:Elder Bloodjaw|Elder Bloodjaws} (plus those from the taints) and summons {creature:Mushroom|Mushrooms} at random around itself throughout the fight (up to 8), which explode after a while or when someone gets close, dealing **2,500+ Life Drain** in a small area.

The Knight uses {spell:Challenge} on all the Elder Bloodjaws and stays in a corner, with a Druid nearby healing him. The room is large: the Paladin runs half a lap on the other side with the boss, and the shooters stay out of the Elder Bloodjaws' sight the whole time (avoiding the 1st taint's position swaps).
As with Murcion: the Paladin runs in a circle with the boss and the Knight runs the full lap with the Elder Bloodjaws, always half a lap behind the Paladin.

Open Ichgahal's corpse. You receive the last taint and 3,250,000 experience. Besides Crystal Coins, potions, gems and ambers, it can drop {item:Ichgahal's Fungal Infestation}, {item:Putrefactive Figurine}, {item:Cursed Wood} (1st Decaying Defender addon), {item:Bag You Covet} and, with the final taint, {item:The Essence of Ichgahal}.

The wiki does not describe the way out: go back to the spot where the {item:Spheric Teleporter} left you and return that way to the Blood Vestibule (or use a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll}). To leave for good, follow the steps “Leave the Blood Vestibule” and “Leave the temple and Drefia” in section 9.

As in the {wiki:Soul War Quest|Soul War Quest}, you can only face {creature:Bakragore} after killing the four children and gathering the four taints. The information below is for the easiest mode (no final taint or burden); with four taints you always receive **+14%** damage, so factor that into all the values.

Make sure **all** members have the four taints. Bakragore is in the Blood Vestibule and you reach it through a lever (the wiki does not give its exact position). You have **25 minutes** to kill it; the boss has 660,000 HP and a cooldown of **2 days and 20 hours**.
Death, Energy, Physical (Paladin and Knight), Life Drain (Knight)
If the team **fails** the fight, it loses the **last two taints** and the progress of **two random bosses** (the same for the whole team). You will have to kill them again.
Elder Bloodjaws, Mushrooms and Mould trails

Bakragore fights with **four** {creature:Elder Bloodjaw|Elder Bloodjaws} and combines its children's mechanics, with important changes. It summons up to 4 {creature:Mushroom|Mushrooms} and leaves trails of {item:Mould (Field)|Mould} wherever it walks: stepping or standing on these trails takes **3% of your maximum health** per second.

You get the white X counter, which rises **2 per second** up to **21**; at most you take **15% of your maximum health** per second. Each step drops a {item:Darkfield} (lasts 3 seconds) and lowers the counter by 1; standing on a Darkfield takes **3% of your maximum health** per second.
Bakragore heals **500 HP** for each Darkfield it steps on.
Avoid the Pillars of Dark Energy

The boss summons up to 4 {creature:Pillar of Dark Energy|Pillars of Dark Energy}, which chain anyone standing next to them with **Death** damage. Whoever is chained gets the red ball counter (maximum 11), which drops by 1 per second and deals **1,500+ Death** on each tick.
Bakragore's beam sets off all those charges at once: a huge Death explosion.

Every **90 seconds** Bakragore drops a {wiki:Rotten Charge|Rotten Charge} in the centre of the room, which immediately deals **1,250 Agony Damage** to everyone and lasts 15 seconds. **If no Elder Bloodjaw steps on it:** warnings at 5 seconds (*"The rotten charge is going to explode!"*) and at 10 (*"THE ROTTEN CHARGE WILL EXPLODE SOON!"*); at 15 it explodes (*"THE ROTTEN ENERGY EXPLODES!"*) and each player loses **80% of their maximum health**. **If an Elder Bloodjaw steps on it**, for 15 seconds: those nearby do not drop Darkfields, the boss does not heal on the fields, the Elder Bloodjaws leave the room and the boss's resistances drop considerably; in return, the boss deals two hits to its current target, at 6 and at 12 seconds.
Unlike its children, Bakragore **does not shout** to warn of its hits. Pay close attention: the Knight must be the target during those 12 seconds.
Defeating Bakragore and receiving the rewards

When Bakragore dies, you receive the **base outfit** {wiki:Decaying Defender Outfits|Decaying Defender}, permission to make {wiki:Crimson Offering|Crimson Offerings} at the Altar in the Blood Vestibule, the **final taint** and 15,000,000 experience. Your normal taints are reset to zero. On the first kill you have an **increased** chance of looting a {item:Bag You Covet}; the chance keeps rising with each kill until you loot it and then goes back to the normal, much lower value. It can also drop {item:Bakragore's Amalgamation}, {item:Figurine of Bakragore}, Promotion Scrolls, {item:Spiritual Horseshoe}, {item:Royal Almandine}, {item:Fiery Tear} and {item:Cobalt Ridge}, as well as Crystal Coins, potions, gems and giant gems.
Decaying Defender base outfit, permission for Crimson Offerings, final taint and 15,000,000 experience
9. After the quest: Crimson Offerings, Burden, taints and exit
With Bakragore defeated you can keep farming the area with the final taint, trade hearts for Sanguine Set pieces and repeat Bakragore at a higher difficulty with better rewards.

While you hunt in the Rotten Blood areas with taints, collect {item:Tainted Heart|Tainted Hearts} and {item:Darklight Heart|Darklight Hearts} (very rare drops). With **5 Tainted Hearts**, **5 Darklight Hearts** and **50,000,000 gp**, talk to the {npc:Altar (NPC)} in the Blood Vestibule: {key:hi}, {key:kneel}, {key:offer} and {key:yes}. You receive a {item:Bag You Covet}, which turns into a piece of the {wiki:Sanguine Set|Sanguine Set}.
Only those who have defeated Bakragore at least once can make offerings.
The final taint and the extra taints

The final taint gives +4.5% experience and loot to you only, with no penalties, and does not count towards the team's taint level. With it, the four children can drop their essences ({item:The Essence of Murcion}, {item:The Essence of Vemiath}, {item:The Essence of Chagorz} and {item:The Essence of Ichgahal}); the more normal taints you have on top, the higher the chance. In boss fights, **the whole team** must have the final taint for this to count.
Extra Elder Bloodjaws in boss fights
Damage taken in the Rotten Blood

If you want to clear your taints (for example to hunt with another team), talk to {npc:A Bloodshade}: {key:hi}, {key:manage}, then {key:lesser} (normal taints only) or {key:great} (the final taint too, and with it all the normal ones) and confirm with {key:yes}.

You can only do this **once every 68 hours** (and only 68 hours after receiving a taint), and it removes **all** taints of that type at once. Also remember that defeating Bakragore resets the normal taints to zero and that losing the fight against it takes the last two from the team.

When **all** members have the four taints **plus** the final taint, pulling Bakragore's lever takes the team to an antechamber (another lever room). You have **3 minutes** to prepare (*"You have only 3 minutes to prepare for the fight. To reset your sacrifice you will have to leave this room and reenter!"*). Anyone who has already consumed an essence (use it to absorb it) can use the {wiki:Bakragore's Burden|Essence Devourer} of that type to sacrifice it (*"The difficulty of the upcoming battle has increased!"*). To recover a consumed essence, use the matching Essence Extractor: it goes back into your backpack.
Player sacrificing the Essence of Ichgahal

Each sacrificed essence replaces an Elder Bloodjaw with an echo of the corresponding child ({creature:Echo of Murcion}, {creature:Echo of Vemiath}, {creature:Echo of Chagorz}, {creature:Echo of Ichgahal}). The echoes do not interact with the trails or the Rotten Charge, disrupt the Elder Bloodjaws' mechanic and do not leave the room with them. The burden only applies to the next fight. It is the only way to get the **Grand Sanguine** weapons and it increases the chance of Sanguine Set pieces and better Promotion Scrolls.

The wiki does not describe the way out of the Blood Vestibule. Go back to where you arrived through the pool of blood (next to {npc:A Bloodshade}) and return that way to A Bloodshade's room in Drefia; if you cannot find a way out, use a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} (you go to your temple and no longer need the next step).
The {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block.

From A Bloodshade's room in Drefia, retrace your path in reverse: leave through the door between the pillars, head **north-east** to the stairs and go up them, climb out of the hole with a {item:Rope}, go up the stairs and pass the Ghouls to the {spell:Levitate} spot, where you go down with *exani hur down*. Then head back **east** across the mountain to the rope spot ({coord:33048,32429,7}) and continue to Darashia, where you take {npc:Petros}'s boat or {npc:Chemar}'s carpet.
You can return to the Blood Vestibule and the four areas (Jaded Roots, Darklight Core, Gloom Pillars and Putrefactory) whenever you want, even after finishing the quest.
If you say {key:blessing} to {npc:A Bloodshade} without having all the taints, he replies that your body and mind are not ready to receive the blessings of the blood god.

The outfit addons come from the {item:Cursed Wood} (Ichgahal) and the {item:Darklight Geode} (Chagorz): you can only use them once you have the base outfit (see the {wiki:Decaying Defender Outfits Quest|Decaying Defender Outfits Quest}). When you have both addons you receive the achievement **Fully Decayed**.
The {item:Bag You Covet} turns into a Sanguine Set piece when you open the reward container. Putting Rotten Blood bosses in the Bosstiary boss slot increases the chance of looting it.
{item:Bloody Tears} drop from the boss {creature:The Fear Feaster}, can be bought on the Market, and {npc:Yasir} buys them for 70,000 gp.
